findings.description: `Can`'s `chosen()` picks the failure-branch content with `failure ?? (typeof fallback === "function" ? null : fallback)`. Nullish coalescing cannot distinguish "failure not supplied" (undefined, which should fall back to `fallback`) from "failure explicitly set to null" (which a caller uses to say 'render nothing on failure even though I have a fallback for plain denial'). Confirmed empirically: rendering `denied-fallback} failure={null}>` against a policy whose evaluation fails shows "denied-fallback" instead of nothing. No test in edges.test.tsx or QadiProvider.test.tsx exercises `failure={null}` together with a non-null `fallback`, so the gap is untested as well as unfixed. Note: spec/behaviors/09-react.md:209's RECOMMENDED note literally specifies `failure ?? fallback`, so the code matches that non-normative spec line, but CanProps' own doc comment ("Defaults to fallback... Supply this to tell them apart") does not disclose that an explicit `null` cannot opt back out once a `fallback` node is set.
findings.suggestedFix: Distinguish "omitted" from "explicitly null" before defaulting, e.g. check `failure !== undefined ? failure : (typeof fallback === "function" ? null : fallback)`, or document plainly on CanProps.failure that passing `null` is equivalent to omitting it and does not suppress a configured `fallback`.

findings.description: The registration effect's dependency array includes `state` (`[instrument, id, kind, atom, state, wraps]`), so every time a gate's decision changes state (Pending->Allowed, Allowed->Rechecking, Rechecking->Denied, etc.) React tears down the previous registration (registerGate's cleanup calls `changed()`) and immediately re-registers (calling `changed()` again). Verified empirically with an instrumented `<Can>` and a controlled resolver: a single Pending->Allowed transition produced 2 `subscribeGates` notifications instead of 1. This only affects `instrument`-enabled trees (opt-in debug/devtools tooling, off by default) and React's own update batching likely coalesces most of the resulting re-renders, so the practical impact is minimal, but it is a real, measurable inefficiency with no test asserting notification counts across a state transition (GateRegistry.test.tsx's notification-count test only covers a same-state re-render).
findings.suggestedFix: Split the identity-lifecycle concern (mount/unmount, which should own registerGate's subscribe/unsubscribe) from the per-render state update (which could mutate the existing GateInstance in the map and call `changed()` once) instead of tearing down and rebuilding the registration on every state change.

findings.description: HydrationCounts.ts is (correctly) left out of src/index.ts's barrel, same as HydrationSeed.ts, HydrationWarning.ts, settled.ts and useGate.ts — but unlike all four of those siblings, its top-of-file doc comment never states that the exclusion is deliberate (AGENTS.md §9). A reader diffing the barrel against src/ has no in-file signal that this omission is intentional scaffolding rather than an oversight, the exact ambiguity the other four files' comments exist to remove.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a short note to HydrationCounts.ts's doc comment (as HydrationSeed.ts and HydrationWarning.ts do) stating it is deliberately out of the barrel per AGENTS.md §9.
